title: Flowering Development, Trichomes and Maturity Heterogeneity
summary: Cannabis reproductive development progresses through observable morphology while glandular trichomes form and mature asynchronously; genotype, age and position prevent one calendar week or color percentage from being universal.

sections.title: Flowering is a developmental transition
sections.body: Photoperiod is a major reproductive signal in conventional photoperiod cannabis, but plants and cultivars can differ in how quickly reproductive morphology appears. Calendar days are useful records but should be interpreted alongside actual floral structures.

sections.title: Trichomes develop through multiple morphological states
sections.body: Cannabis inflorescences bear several glandular trichome types and capitate trichomes change in stalk formation, head appearance, resin production and senescence across flower development. These structures are central sites of cannabinoid and terpene accumulation.

sections.title: Maturity is heterogeneous
sections.body: Research found trichome number and maturation differed by genotype and plant age and that structures within the same inflorescence can be at different maturity stages. Representative sampling is therefore more defensible than a universal clear-cloudy-amber percentage rule.
